note: Authored source-level extraction BEFORE candidate synthesis. No estimate is converted to a graph coefficient. Separate contrasts from one study are not replications.

findings.locator: PubMed abstract; PMC indexed methods and General Discussion
findings.design: Randomized prior exposure to headlines; study-level allocation details not fully re-extracted
findings.population: Online MTurk participants; fake-news headline tasks, not a representative population
findings.sample: Two preregistered experiments reported more than 1,800 participants in indexed discussion; no aggregate sample recomputed
findings.context: Headlines presented in a social-media-like format
findings.exposure: Prior encounter with a specified headline
findings.comparator: Previously unexposed headline at truth assessment
findings.measurement: Perceived accuracy of the claim, not objective truth or source trust
findings.timing: Same session and reported one-week retest
findings.result: Previously presented fake-news headlines received higher accuracy ratings; no generalized monotonic dose function established.
findings.limitations: Low absolute believability; convenience sample; truth-rating operationalization; no evidence for arbitrary repeated content or real-world behavioral consequences.

findings.locator: PubMed abstract: entirely implausible statements contrast
findings.context: Statements such as geometrically impossible descriptions
findings.timing: Reported test interval; exact interval not extracted for this contrast
findings.result: The source reports no repetition effect for entirely implausible statements.
findings.limitations: No equivalence margin or precision assessment extracted; non-detection does not prove a zero effect.

findings.locator: Abstract; Results: Study Characteristics and Publication Bias; Introduction boundary discussion
findings.population: Predominantly European/North American research settings; heterogeneous claim materials
findings.exposure: Repeated presentation under study-specific initial tasks
findings.comparator: Novel statements or aligned pre/post criteria
findings.measurement: Truth ratings; synthesis distinguishes different comparison criteria
findings.timing: Study-dependent initial exposure and later test
findings.result: Positive bias-adjusted pooled repetition effect with substantial heterogeneity; initial task and veracity cues matter.
findings.limitations: Small-study effects, non-equivalent materials, possible overlapping components; not a universal dose-response or an independent replication of included trials.

findings.locator: Indexed publisher/PMC abstract and results: initial accuracy versus interestingness judgments
findings.design: Lab-in-field and online experiments; task instruction contrasts
findings.population: Professional content moderators and separate India/Philippines general-population samples
findings.sample: Reported second moderator experiment N=239; general samples India 997, Philippines 1,184; not pooled here
findings.exposure: Initial accuracy judgment before repeated exposure
findings.result: Accuracy-focused initial processing attenuated the adverse repetition pattern reported in comparison tasks.
findings.limitations: Only indexed excerpts accessed; no exact zero/equivalence claim; occupation and countries constrain transfer; possible overlap with 2026 synthesis.

findings.locator: Methods Participants; Results H1a, Experiment 2 conditions 1 versus 2 and baseline-adjusted belief-change contrast
findings.design: Randomized online correction-format comparison; analytic Experiment 2 N=369
findings.population: Adult US MTurk sample, not population-representative
findings.sample: Experiment 2 N=369 overall, including other conditions
findings.context: Specified short false claims previously presented
findings.comparator: Plain false-tag retraction of the same claim
findings.measurement: 0–10 belief truth rating of the same false proposition
findings.result: Refutation produced lower false-claim belief than plain retraction in the previously exposed conditions; baseline-adjusted change supported the contrast.
findings.limitations: Bundled wording/reasons/source information; attrition and convenience sample; inferential reasoning is a separate outcome, not the Driver itself.

findings.locator: Abstract and Results H1a: Experiment 1 one-day contrast
findings.design: Randomized correction-format contrast; no-exposure control separately recruited
findings.sample: Experiment 1 N=531 overall including nonrandom no-exposure group; that group not used as randomized evidence here
findings.result: No detected refutation advantage for direct belief ratings at one day; inference findings are not substituted for this null contrast.
findings.limitations: No equivalence margin; nonsignificance is not evidence of zero or equivalence. Does not negate the separately scoped week result.

findings.locator: PubMed abstract: pooled effect and moderator summary
findings.result: Pooled average was not statistically distinguishable from zero; detail/topic/polarization varied with correction success.
findings.limitations: Not a direct refutation-versus-retraction replication; interval spans negative and positive values; no supported-null conclusion; included-study overlap unresolved.

findings.locator: PubMed PMID35144111 / Europe PMC indexed abstract, preregistered experiment and exploratory heterogeneity
findings.design: Preregistered repeated-versus-new highly implausible statement experiment; allocation details not re-extracted from abstract
findings.population: Statement-judgment participants; demographic/sample-transfer detail not extracted
findings.context: Highly implausible statements assessed with 100-point truth scale
findings.measurement: Rated truth, not objective accuracy or acceptance above midpoint
findings.timing: Five presentations before judgment; exact delay not extracted
findings.result: Repeated highly implausible statements received higher truth ratings than new statements, still below the scale midpoint. Exploratory results showed about half of participants with no or reversed pattern.
findings.limitations: Contradicts a universal extreme-implausibility exclusion, not the bounded 2018 null contrast. Exposure count and scale sensitivity differ; neither moderator is independently isolated here. Preprint and published version are one work. Possible inclusion in later synthesis is not independent replication.

assertions.scope: Repeated encounter with the same factual statement/headline can alter subsequently rated belief confidence in controlled adult online/laboratory tasks. Ordinary judgment tasks often show increases; extreme implausibility, explicit veracity cues and initial accuracy focus bound the claim. No universal monotonic sign, transfer to arbitrary content, calibrated truth or behavior is asserted. Extreme implausibility is not a universal exclusion: a later five-presentation/100-point-scale experiment found higher ratings while ratings remained below midpoint.
assertions.mechanism: Repeated encounters may supply processing familiarity/fluency or memory-reference cues interpreted during truth judgment. Competing mechanisms remain unresolved; no mediating pathway asserted.
assertions.rationale: Experimental exposure precedes truth judgment; converging synthesis retains heterogeneity and small-study limitations. No causal inference from familiarity ratings alone.

assertions.scope: Same factual headline/claim repeated within a declared initial-task and test protocol; target is belief confidence in that claim, not its objective accuracy. Ordinary initial tasks can increase rated truth; accuracy-focused instructions, veracity cues and implausibility can attenuate or remove detected effects. No arbitrary dose-response. Extreme implausibility is not a universal exclusion: a later five-presentation/100-point-scale experiment found higher ratings while ratings remained below midpoint.
assertions.timing: Initial exposure before later judgment; same-session or measured delays only
assertions.measurement: Truth/accuracy rating of the specified claim; not source trust, calibration or behavioral compliance
assertions.mechanism: Encounter history changes available judgment cues; fluency versus referential explanation is not resolved.
assertions.rationale: Scoped empirical effect with explicit non-universal direction and null boundary findings; this is the same exposure contribution as the candidate Relationship, not an additional causal input.
assertions.risk: Do not operationally spread misinformation. Scientific observation does not authorize deception, targeting, practitioner use or platform intervention.

assertions.scope: For previously exposed short false claims in the reported adult US MTurk protocol, explanatory refutation versus plain false-tag retraction reduced belief in the same false proposition at approximately one week. This comparison is not a universal effect of any correction or a one-day benefit.
assertions.timing: Approximately one-week comparison; one-day null contrast preserved independently
assertions.measurement: 0–10 direct truth-belief rating; inferential reasoning is separate and not promoted to belief confidence
assertions.mechanism: Refutation supplies a corrected account/reasons that can compete with the original claim; individual component mechanisms and mediation are not identified.
assertions.rationale: Exact randomized format contrast survives boundary review. Broader correction synthesis is mixed; its overlap and broader estimand prevent pooling it as an independent replication.
assertions.risk: Require accurate correction and relevant sources; no guaranteed acceptance, confidence calibration, accuracy benefit for other claims or permission to manipulate audiences.

happeningTypes.name: Present a specified claim again in a bounded exposure protocol
happeningTypes.description: Arrange a further encounter with the same specified claim/headline under an explicit presentation protocol. Identity records presentation only, not belief, truth, efficacy or permission.
happeningTypes.constraints: Specified content, consent, provenance, harm/ethics and lawful authority are unassessed. No misinformation deployment authorized.

happeningTypes.name: Present a concise explanatory refutation of a specified false claim
happeningTypes.description: Present a short message identifying a particular false claim and supplying a corrected account with reasons/source context. Treat the message protocol as a bundle; identity implies no efficacy or component effect.
happeningTypes.constraints: Claim status and corrected account require verification; applicability, feasibility, legal, ethical and actor control assessments remain unassessed.
